name: Double Sir (Court Piece)
description: Double Sir (also known as Double Sar or Double Sir-Bandi) is a popular and strategic variant of Court Piece (Rang) played extensively in India and Pakistan. It is a trickndtaking game for four players in fixed partnerships. The defining feature of Double Sir is that a player can only capture tricks from the table if they win two consecutive tricks, adding a layered tactical challenge to standard whist-style play.

history.origins: Double Sir is a regional evolution of the classic 'Court Piece' (or Rang), which traces its roots to 19thndcentury Whist. It is particularly associated with the Punjab region and North India.
timeline: 1800s: Standard Whist variants spread throughout South Asia during British colonial rule.
Early 20th Century: The 'Double' consecutivendwin rule emerges as a way to make the game more challenging and lengthy.
Modern Era: One of the most common street and social card games in Pakistan and Northern India.
history.cultural: Highly social, often played in public squares, tea stalls (dhabas), and during festivals.
history.evolution: The name 'Sir' or 'Sar' comes from the Hindi/Urdu word for 'Head' or 'Win'. Providing a 'Double Sir' refers to the requirement of two consecutive trick wins to clear the table.

setup.deck: Standard 52ndcard deck. Aces are high (A, K, Q, J, 10... 2).
setup.dealing: Dealer is chosen by lot. Dealer deals 5 cards to each player. The player to the dealer's right (the 'Trump Caller') chooses the trump suit. Then the dealer deals the remaining cards in batches of 4.

rules.objective: Capture as many tricks as possible. The team that wins at least 7 of the 13 tricks wins the round.
rules.gameplay:
1. Standard Trick Play: The trump caller leads the first trick. Players must follow suit if possible.
2. The Consecutive Rule: Tricks are NOT picked up after each round. They remain face down in a pile in the center of the table.
3. Capturing: To pick up the pile of tricks, the same player (not just the same team) must win TWO consecutive tricks. When that happens, that player's team collects the entire centre pile.
4. Reset: Once the tricks are collected, the pile in the center is empty. The winner of the last trick leads the next.
keyRules: The 13th trick is always collected by the winner of that trick, along with any remaining cards in the center pile.
Only the same player (not the partner) winning two consecutive tricks may collect the centre pile.
If tricks 1-12 are not collected (no one wins two in a row), the winner of the 13th trick takes the entire board (very rare).

strategy.basic: If your partner has won a trick and it is sitting in the center, play your best cards to help them win the very next trick for a doublendwin.
strategy.intermediate: Trump Control: Use your small trumps to 'break' the opponent's consecutive win. If an opponent wins a trick, use a trump on the next trick even if it's unlikely to win the whole round, just to prevent them from getting two in a row.
strategy.advanced: Baiting: Intentionally play a mediocre card after your team has won a trick to bait the opponent into overplaying, then counter with a high trump to secure the consecutive win.
tips: The first 5 cards are the most important for choosing the trump suit. Choose a suit where you have high honors (Ace/King).
Pay attention to the center pileâ€”the bigger the pile, the more aggressive you should be with your high cards.

variations.name: No pick-up for first two tricks
variations.description: A player who wins the first two tricks cannot pick them up; a player who wins the second and third tricks can pick up the three tricks as usual.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation changes pick-up rules only; no engine constant overrides documented in sources.

variations.name: No pick-up for 11th and 12th
variations.description: A player who wins the 11th and 12th tricks cannot pick up the tricks from the table, making it harder to escape a court.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation changes pick-up rules only; no engine constant overrides documented in sources.

variations.name: Goon court counts 10
variations.description: Some play that a goon court (dealer's team wins every trick) counts as 10 courts rather than three.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation changes court count for goon; no engine constant overrides documented in sources.
